text:
# Agent Hub policy floor. Lives in the APP repo: it is not content and not editable through the API/UI.
# Content (rules, MCP items, profiles) may only be STRICTER than this file; the planner turns any violation into a
# structured finding and blocks apply for that client. Change it in git, with review, like any security control.
version: 1

# Egress is deny-by-default. Content can only add explicit `egress_host allow` rules for named hosts.
network_default: deny
egress:
  forbid_allow_patterns: ["*", "*.*", "**"]     # a catch-all host allow is an egress hole
  forbid_allow_probes: ["a", "a.b", "example.com", "example.io", "example.org", "example.dev", "example.net", "a.b.c.d"]   # an allow pattern that matches any probe is a catch-all in disguise
  loopback_hosts: ["127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"]

# Hard denies: content can never allow a read/write that overlaps these (paths are globs; ~ is the home dir).
deny_path_read:
  - "~/.ssh/**"
  - "~/.aws/**"
  - "~/.config/gcloud/**"
  - "~/.gnupg/**"
  - "~/.netrc"
  - "~/.config/google-chrome/**"
  - "~/.config/chromium/**"
  - "~/.config/BraveSoftware/**"
  - "~/.mozilla/**"
  - "~/snap/firefox/**"
  - "~/snap/chromium/**"
  - "~/.local/share/keyrings/**"
  - "~/.config/agent-hub/**"
  - "~/.local/share/agent-hub/**"       # hub state: keys, DB, backups, locks, plans (data_dir is added at runtime too)
  - "~/.config/agent-knowledge/**"
  - "~/.local/share/agent-knowledge/**"
  - "**/bootstrap-admin.key"
  - "**/admin.key"
  - "**/.env"
deny_path_write:
  - "~/.ssh/**"
  - "~/.aws/**"
  - "~/.config/gcloud/**"
  - "~/.gnupg/**"
  - "~/.netrc"
  - "~/.config/agent-hub/**"
  - "~/.local/share/agent-hub/**"       # hub state: keys, DB, backups, locks, plans
  - "~/.config/agent-knowledge/**"
  - "~/.local/share/agent-knowledge/**"
  - "**/bootstrap-admin.key"
  - "**/admin.key"

# Per-tool posture. `default` applies when no content rule names the tool; `max` is the most permissive decision
# content may grant (deny < ask < allow). web tools are off by default and can at most be "ask".
tools:
  web_fetch: {default: deny, max: ask}
  web_search: {default: deny, max: ask}
  shell: {default: ask, max: ask}       # a bare `allow` for shell is never valid; use a `command` rule with a pattern
default_tool_decision: ask

# `allow` on a command rule needs a real pattern (never a catch-all).
command_allow_forbid_patterns: ["*", "**", "*.*", "?*", ".*"]
command_allow_probes: ["a", "a b", "a b c", "a.b.c", "sh -c x", "bash -c x", "docker compose up", "docker run x", "python x.py",
                       "python3 x", "sudo x", "rm -rf /"]   # matching any of these = a catch-all
# general-purpose launchers: an allow that matches one is a WARNING (a bare wildcard is already an error above)
command_allow_warn_probes: ["git x", "node x", "npx x", "uv run x", "uvx x", "find x", "xargs x", "perl x", "awk x", "env x", "nohup x",
                            "timeout x", "ssh x", "curl x", "wget x"]

mcp:
  require_scan_clean: true              # scan_status must be `clean` before an MCP server may be enabled
  require_explicit_egress: true         # every egress host must be covered by an explicit egress_host allow rule

# Example spec: adjust to your client's current config format. Covers .cursor/mcp.json with `mcpServers` and AGENTS.md at
# the project root. Check the paths before enabling `manage`.
# Its job is to prove that a new client needs a spec, not code.
id: cursor
adapter: generic
display_name: Cursor (example spec)
description: Instructions into AGENTS.md (hub block) and MCP servers into .cursor/mcp.json. Skills/agents are not mapped.
strict: false
roots:
  project: ~/path/to/project
manage: {skills: false, agents: false, instructions: true, mcp: false, permissions: false, memory: false}
spec:
  version: 1
  notes: Example spec. Cursor rules (.cursor/rules/*.mdc) are not mapped; add an `agents`-style section if you need them.
  instructions:
    root: project
    file: AGENTS.md
    mode: block
  mcp:
    root: project
    file: .cursor/mcp.json
    format: json
    key_path: mcpServers
    env_style: dollar_brace
    entry:
      stdio: {command: "{command}", args: "{args}", env: "{env}"}
      http: {url: "{url}"}
      sse: {url: "{url}"}

# Example spec: adjust to your client's current config format. Covers project AGENTS.md, and MCP servers
# as [mcp_servers.<name>] tables in a config.toml. The TOML table is delivered as a hub marker block (no TOML key-merge exists).
# `roots.codex_home` must be the directory that holds config.toml on your machine.
id: codex-cli
adapter: generic
display_name: Codex CLI (example spec)
description: AGENTS.md block, skills as dir-per-skill, MCP tables in config.toml (marker block).
strict: false
roots:
  project: ~/path/to/project
  codex_home: ~/.codex
manage: {skills: false, agents: false, instructions: true, mcp: false, permissions: false, memory: false}
spec:
  version: 1
  notes: Example spec. Drop the skills section if your Codex does not read that location.
  skills:
    root: codex_home
    path: skills
    layout: dir_per_skill
    filename: SKILL.md
  instructions:
    root: project
    file: AGENTS.md
    mode: block
  mcp:
    root: codex_home
    file: config.toml
    format: toml
    key_path: mcp_servers
    env_style: names_only
    entry:
      stdio: {command: "{command}", args: "{args}"}
      http: {url: "{url}"}

# Example spec: adjust to your client's current config format. Covers the GEMINI.md context file and .gemini/settings.json
# with `mcpServers` (`httpUrl` for streamable HTTP, `url` for SSE).
id: gemini-cli
adapter: generic
display_name: Gemini CLI (example spec)
description: GEMINI.md (whole file hub-owned) and MCP servers in .gemini/settings.json.
strict: false
roots:
  project: ~/path/to/project
manage: {skills: false, agents: false, instructions: true, mcp: false, permissions: false, memory: false}
spec:
  version: 1
  notes: Example spec.
  instructions:
    root: project
    file: GEMINI.md
    mode: own
  mcp:
    root: project
    file: .gemini/settings.json
    format: json
    key_path: mcpServers
    env_style: dollar_brace
    entry:
      stdio: {command: "{command}", args: "{args}", env: "{env}"}
      http: {httpUrl: "{url}"}
      sse: {url: "{url}"}

text:
# Agent Hub policy floor. Lives in the APP repo: it is not content and not editable through the API/UI.
# Content (rules, MCP items, profiles) may only be STRICTER than this file; the planner turns any violation into a
# structured finding and blocks apply for that client. Change it in git, with review, like any security control.
version: 1

# Egress is deny-by-default. Content can only add explicit `egress_host allow` rules for named hosts.
network_default: deny
egress:
  forbid_allow_patterns: ["*", "*.*", "**"]     # a catch-all host allow is an egress hole
  forbid_allow_probes: ["a", "a.b", "example.com", "example.io", "example.org", "example.dev", "example.net", "a.b.c.d"]   # an allow pattern that matches any probe is a catch-all in disguise
  loopback_hosts: ["127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"]

# Hard denies: content can never allow a read/write that overlaps these (paths are globs; ~ is the home dir).
deny_path_read:
  - "~/.ssh/**"
  - "~/.aws/**"
  - "~/.config/gcloud/**"
  - "~/.gnupg/**"
  - "~/.netrc"
  - "~/.config/google-chrome/**"
  - "~/.config/chromium/**"
  - "~/.config/BraveSoftware/**"
  - "~/.mozilla/**"
  - "~/snap/firefox/**"
  - "~/snap/chromium/**"
  - "~/.local/share/keyrings/**"
  - "~/.docker/**"                      # registry credentials (config.json)
  - "~/.kube/**"                        # cluster credentials
  - "~/.git-credentials"
  - "~/.config/gh/**"                   # GitHub CLI token
  - "~/.npmrc"                          # registry tokens
  - "~/.config/agent-hub/**"
  - "~/.local/share/agent-hub/**"       # hub state: keys, DB, backups, locks, plans (data_dir is added at runtime too)
  - "~/.config/agent-knowledge/**"
  - "~/.local/share/agent-knowledge/**"
  - "**/bootstrap-admin.key"
  - "**/admin.key"
  - "**/.env"
deny_path_write:
  - "~/.ssh/**"
  - "~/.aws/**"
  - "~/.config/gcloud/**"
  - "~/.gnupg/**"
  - "~/.netrc"
  - "~/.config/agent-hub/**"
  - "~/.local/share/agent-hub/**"       # hub state: keys, DB, backups, locks, plans
  - "~/.config/agent-knowledge/**"
  - "~/.local/share/agent-knowledge/**"
  - "**/bootstrap-admin.key"
  - "**/admin.key"

# Per-tool posture. `default` applies when no content rule names the tool; `max` is the most permissive decision
# content may grant (deny < ask < allow). web tools are off by default and can at most be "ask".
tools:
  web_fetch: {default: deny, max: ask}
  web_search: {default: deny, max: ask}
  shell: {default: ask, max: ask}       # a bare `allow` for shell is never valid; use a `command` rule with a pattern
default_tool_decision: ask

# `allow` on a command rule needs a real pattern (never a catch-all).
command_allow_forbid_patterns: ["*", "**", "*.*", "?*", ".*"]
command_allow_probes: ["a", "a b", "a b c", "a.b.c", "sh -c x", "bash -c x", "docker compose up", "docker run x", "python x.py",
                       "python3 x", "sudo x", "rm -rf /"]   # matching any of these = a catch-all
# general-purpose launchers: an allow that matches one is a WARNING (a bare wildcard is already an error above)
command_allow_warn_probes: ["git x", "node x", "npx x", "uv run x", "uvx x", "find x", "xargs x", "perl x", "awk x", "env x", "nohup x",
                            "timeout x", "ssh x", "curl x", "wget x"]

mcp:
  require_scan_clean: true              # scan_status must be `clean` before an MCP server may be enabled
  require_explicit_egress: true         # every egress host must be covered by an explicit egress_host allow rule

# Config for the containerised agent-knowledge in docker-compose.broker.yml (template).
host: 0.0.0.0                     # only with --allow-bind-any, only on an internal network
port: 8795
allowed_hosts: ["agent-knowledge:8795"]   # Host header the broker sends (DNS-rebinding allowlist)
data_dir: /data
lance_dir: /data/lance
# qdrant_url: http://qdrant:6333
router_url: http://router:4000            # any OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint (e.g. a LiteLLM router); reach it via your own broker
                                          # (also overridable with the env var KNOWLEDGE_ROUTER_URL)
router_api_key_env: KNOWLEDGE_EMBED_API_KEY   # env var NAME (an embeddings-only router VIRTUAL key, never the master key); value comes from env, never written here
qdrant_api_key_env: KNOWLEDGE_QDRANT_API_KEY  # only used when qdrant_url is set
default_embedding_model: text-embedding-3-small   # example; use a model your endpoint serves
ingest_roots: []                          # no host filesystem is mounted, so path ingest is off

description: Builds things.
